clue.text: Skill in designing board game — piece on the board's with it

parts.note: draughts is the British name for checkers
a man is a playing piece in draughts or chess; the 's gives the S
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at designing board games is told a piece on the board is with it.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAUGHTS is the British name for checkers, and MAN'S gives MANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmanship is the craft of technical drawing, the skill behind any design.

clue.text: Assault school's leader and punishment is to be reported

parts.note: to hit is to assault
the head is the headteacher who leads a school
lines are a school punishment: writing a sentence over and over

explanation.surface: A pupil who attacks the headteacher and is punished ends up in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools 'lines' is a punishment where a pupil copies a sentence many times.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the headlines is an idiom for becoming front-page news, being widely reported.

clue.text: Engineers made oddly smooth info for IT user

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: made arranged oddly signals its letters are jumbled

parts.note: to file something is to smooth it with a file

explanation.surface: Engineers have produced some strangely polished information for a computer user.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' makes ADME from MADE; 'oddly' might suggest alternate letters, but here it means strangely arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A readme file is a text document shipped with software giving users essential information.

clue.text: Specialist on staff cheers up, given facial adornment

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word for cheers is written bottom to top

parts.note: ta is a British informal word for thanks, like cheers
tache is short for moustache

explanation.surface: A staff member brightens up after growing a beard or moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TA into AT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a diplomat with a specialist area, such as a military or cultural attaché on an embassy's staff.

clue.text: Fans removing clothing in part of game

indicators.note: stripping the clothes off a word means taking away its outer letters

parts.note: lovers of something are its fans

explanation.surface: Fans stripping off during a match, a familiar sporting scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing clothing' strips L and S from LOVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end, a division of play.

clue.text: During school, outcast turned up advanced means of deterring pests

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a school of thought is a sect

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word for outcast is read bottom to top

parts.note: a leper is a social outcast
money advanced is money lent

explanation.surface: A shunned pupil rises in school and lends a hand to keep pests away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns LEPER into REPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect repellent is a substance applied to keep biting bugs away.

clue.text: Involved in anarchism, need lingo of Communists

indicators.note: involved in the sense of twisted or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Anarchists need a language, the tongue of their Communist rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' scrambles IN, ANARCHISM and NEED together; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the official language of the People's Republic of China, run by the Communist Party.

clue.text: One falters lamely, being so?

indicators.note: doing something lamely means doing it haltingly and badly, so the letters stumble into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles weakly, presumably because they are the weakest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamely' scrambles I and FALTERS; the whole clue also describes the answer, since one who is frailest falters.
explanation.definitionFit: The frailest person is the weakest, the most likely to falter and walk lamely.

clue.text: Picaroon stops craving lucre, which is forgivable

indicators.note: stops in the sense of plugging a gap, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: venal means open to bribery, greedy for money
the setter's name, so I, the setter speaking

explanation.surface: The setter plugs a mercenary streak, which is a pardonable fault.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often clue themselves as I or ME; here the setter's pseudonym Picaroon gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin is a minor one that can be pardoned, as opposed to a mortal sin.

clue.text: Disapproved of skirt shortened by 1950s' teenager

indicators.note: a shortened word loses its last letter, as a hem is taken up

parts.note: a tutu is a ballerina's skirt
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a British 1950s youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: Someone frowned on a teenage Teddy boy's taste for short skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths who wore Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut is to click the tongue in disapproval, so tutted means showed disapproval.

clue.text: Broadcast publicity about horrible vacuous fools

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pieces go round the next

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
ads are advertisements, publicity

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the outer letters of horrible remain

explanation.surface: Awful advertising on the airwaves is aimed at brainless idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' looks like it describes the fools, but it empties 'horrible' to its outer letters, and 'about' places those inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is a slang term for an empty-headed, silly person, a fool.

clue.text: Excited remark from man entertained by compilers

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: setters, as crossword compilers, call themselves we
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man is having fun with crossword setters and lets out a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Whee is an exclamation of delight or exhilaration, such as on a fairground ride.

clue.text: Old Scottish side admitting wild riot in showers

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Hibs is the nickname of Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of riot running amok

explanation.surface: A former Scottish football team let in a riot during the downpours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' makes ITOR from RIOT. 'showers' looks like rain, but it means people who show things.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhibitors are people who display things at shows, so they are showers (rhymes with 'mowers').

clue.text: Old issue, either of two in Marxism-Leninism?

definitions.meaning: a past issue of a magazine
Marxism and Leninism both end in M, the Roman numeral for a thousand: a number at the back

explanation.surface: An old magazine article on a two-part communist doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: each word of Marxism-Leninism ends with M, a Roman numeral, so each has a number at its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is an earlier edition of a periodical, and figuratively anything outdated.

clue.text: Daisy knocked over football team's comic character

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the team's letters run backwards

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A girl called Daisy was knocked over by a football side's funny mascot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns XI into IX.
explanation.definitionFit: Asterix is the little Gaulish warrior hero of the French comic book series.

clue.text: Televises bits of rock by pair of players

parts.note: scree is loose fragments of rock on a slope
in bridge North and South are partners, N and S

explanation.surface: A television channel shows pieces of rock music by a duo.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South are a partnership in bridge, a standard crossword source of N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a programme is to show it on television, so screens means televises.

clue.text: What follows 19 is to confuse revolutionary

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle them
Trot is short for Trotskyist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: The answer to clue 19 is a puzzle to a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, Echo (the answer to 19) is followed by Foxtrot.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio alphabet Foxtrot is the code word for F, coming right after Echo for E.

clue.text: Old garment from clothes shop with vulture's tail feathers

parts.note: H&M is a clothing retailer, written out as H and M

indicators.note: a creature's tail is its end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: An old item of clothing from a fashion store trimmed with vulture feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: H&M, the high-street fashion chain, is read as H AND M.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-me-down is a used garment passed on from one wearer, often an older sibling, to another.

clue.text: Husband clad in green waves coming back

indicators.note: clad in means dressed in, so the husband is wrapped by the green

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: A husband dressed in green watches the waves roll back.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is sound waves bouncing back off a surface to the listener.

clue.text: Like irrational tirade for an ambitious type

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
pi is an irrational number
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: An unreasonable outburst is typical of a pushy go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' is not an anagram signal here: pi is the classic irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone who aspires to a goal or position, an ambitious person.

clue.text: Perhaps pretentious political group out of power

indicators.note: out of means without, so the letter for power leaves the group

parts.note: a party is a political group
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A political group thrown out of office might be seen as affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes something with artistic pretensions; pretentious is one example of that, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Billionaire into S&M rejected seedy things

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
rejected means sent back, so S&M is read backwards

parts.note: sadomasochism, abbreviated S and M
Elon Musk is a famous billionaire

explanation.surface: A billionaire who was into sadomasochism has turned away from such sleazy pursuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SM into MS. 'seedy' suggests sleaze, but means full of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Melons are fruits packed with seeds, so literally seedy things.

clue.text: Strip joint that's sordid by street

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club

explanation.surface: A strip club that is seedy, down by the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip someone of possessions or clothing.

clue.text: Writer wearing nothing with cape is being revealing

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the nought comes on to the front of the writer

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a pen is a writing instrument
ness is a headland, a cape

explanation.surface: A naked author in only a cloak is showing rather a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts O on before PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Openness is frankness, the quality of disclosing things freely.
